title: Dynamic Reservation Orchestrator with Predictive Buffering
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
Problem: Customers buying Dedicated capacity need predictable throughput guarantees but often experience overprovisioning or unexpected throttling when burst patterns occur. Current reservation intake and approval flows are manual-heavy and do not account for short-term burst risk, leading to SLA violations or conservative capacity commitments that increase cost.

Goal: Build a Dynamic Reservation Orchestrator that combines reservation requests, approval policies, autoscaling guardrails, and a predictive burst buffer so we can: (1) reduce conservative overcommit by 15-30%, (2) maintain SLA adherence for P99 latency and throughput, and (3) automate approval recommendations for capacity planners and sales engineers.

Scope: This ticket covers the end-to-end provisioning workflow changes and orchestration logic for Dedicated reservations: intake normalization, predicted burst estimator, temporary buffer allocation (soft burst pool), approval recommendation UI + API, and controls to bind autoscale policies to reservations.
acceptance_criteria: Reservation intake UI accepts workload profile and historical token/day distribution; normalizes to a standard schema
Predictive burst estimator trained on anonymized historical telemetry returns 95th percentile burst request capacity for the next 30-day horizon
Orchestrator can allocate a soft burst buffer from a shared pool and attach it to a reservation with a TTL and conditional billing adjustments
Approval recommendation engine surfaces a green/yellow/red signal plus rationale (utilization, burst risk, cost delta) in the Console for reviewer
Autoscaling policies can be linked to reservation objects and enforce max scaling bounds and cooldowns; policy attachments survive model rollouts and region failovers
E2E integration test demonstrating no SLA regression on a representative workload (P99 latency within SLA) using canary fleet
Documentation (runbook + intake form spec) published and linked from Console reservation flow
notes_and_decisions: Use a hybrid approach: deterministic business rules (commit windows, reserved throughput floors) plus ML-driven burst estimator to reduce black-box behavior
Soft burst buffer is charged at a premium usage rate and reclaimed automatically after TTL; customers see a projected cost delta in approval UI
Autoscale policy primitives: min_reserved, target_throughput, hard_cap, cooldown_seconds, fallback_model_variant
We will initially enable soft burst buffers only in Hosted and Dedicated regions in NA and EU; APAC rollout deferred to a follow-up
To avoid regulatory issues, predictive estimator will run on aggregated/anonymized telemetry and will be opt-out by enterprise customers who require data isolation
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (design): finalize intake schema and approval decision matrix — 2 weeks
Phase 1 (backend): implement orchestrator service, reservation object model, and autoscale policy binding — 4 weeks
Phase 2 (predictive): train and validate burst estimator on historical dedicated tenant telemetry; expose estimator API — 3 weeks
Phase 3 (console + API): approval UI, recommended decisions, and pricing delta preview — 2 weeks
Phase 4 (canary): enable for 5 pilot customers with SE support; monitor cost and SLA metrics — 4 weeks
Phase 5 (general availability): iterate on controls, expand region support, and publish runbook — 2 weeks
metrics: Delta in committed capacity versus actual utilization (target: -20% conservative overcommit reduction)
Incident count where reservation-related throughput breaches SLA (target: 0 for GA customers; <2 for pilots)
False positive approval rejections vs manual overrides (target: <10%)
Average time to approve reservation with recommendation (target: <12 hours)
Customer reported satisfaction (qual survey) for provisioning UX (target: 4/5)
Cost uplift from soft burst buffer usage (tracked as % of monthly invoice)
Predictive estimator accuracy at 95th percentile for 30-day burst horizon (target: >=85%)
